seoDescription: Learn how to quickly create a powerful admin panel in your Laravel project using the Open Admin package. This step-by-step guide covers the entire process, from creating a new Laravel application and running database migrations to installing Open Admin with just a few commands. Discover how to use the helper scaffolding tool to instantly generate models, controllers, and menu items for your database tables, enabling full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) functionality, including file uploads, right out of the box.

chapters.title: Introduction & Project Setup
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the Open Admin panel that will be created and walks through the initial setup of a fresh Laravel project.

chapters.title: Database Migration and Verification
chapters.description: This chapter covers creating a database and running the initial migrations to set up the default Laravel tables.

chapters.title: Automated Database Creation
chapters.description: This section shows how Artisan can automatically create a database if one doesn't exist and then verifies the new tables in phpMyAdmin.

chapters.title: Installing the Open Admin Package
chapters.description: This chapter walks through the three primary commands required to install the Open Admin package into the Laravel project.

chapters.title: First Login and Dashboard Overview
chapters.description: This part covers logging into the new admin panel for the first time and getting a brief tour of the initial dashboard.

chapters.title: Installing the Helper Scaffolding Tool
chapters.description: This chapter introduces and installs the Open Admin Helper scaffolding extension, which simplifies creating new admin sections.

chapters.title: Scaffolding a New 'Student' Resource
chapters.description: The video walks through using the scaffold tool to generate a new model, controller, migration, and menu item for a 'Student' resource.

chapters.title: Configuring File System and Creating Data
chapters.description: This chapter covers the necessary filesystem configuration for file uploads and then demonstrates creating a new student record directly from the admin panel.

chapters.title: Fixing Image Display in Forms and Lists
chapters.description: This section troubleshoots and fixes two issues: images not appearing in the edit form due to an incorrect APP_URL, and images not rendering in the main data grid.

chapters.title: Scaffolding an Existing 'User' Model
chapters.description: The tutorial demonstrates how to use the scaffolding tool for an existing model and table, like Laravel's default User model.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Final Thoughts
chapters.description: The video concludes by briefly mentioning roles and permissions and summarizing the benefits of using Open Admin for Laravel projects.

summary:
## Overview
This guide demonstrates how to quickly add a feature-rich admin panel to a Laravel project using the **Open Admin** package. The process involves installing the package, using a helper tool for scaffolding, and making minor configuration adjustments for full functionality.

## Core Installation Steps
To get the basic admin panel running, follow these command-line steps in your Laravel project root:

1.  **Require the Package:**
    ```bash
    composer require open-admin-org/open-admin
    ```
2.  **Publish Assets:**
    ```bash
    php artisan vendor:publish --provider="OpenAdmin\Admin\AdminServiceProvider"
    ```
3.  **Install Admin Panel (Creates tables & user):**
    ```bash
    php artisan admin:install
    ```

> [!NOTE]
> After installation, you can log in at `/admin` with the default credentials:
> - **Username:** `admin`
> - **Password:** `admin`

## Helper Scaffolding for Rapid Development
For an even faster workflow, install the **helper scaffolding** tool. This allows you to generate complete admin sections (controllers, menus, etc.) through a web interface.

1.  **Require the Helper Package:**
    ```bash
    composer require open-admin-ext/helpers
    ```
2.  **Import the Helper into Admin:**
    ```bash
    php artisan admin:import helpers
    ```

This adds a **Helpers** menu to your admin panel.

## Scaffolding Examples

### Creating a New Resource (e.g., 'Student')
1.  Navigate to **Helpers > Scaffolding**.
2.  Define the **Table name** (e.g., `students`), **Model** (`Student`), and **Controller** (`StudentController`).
3.  Add the desired fields (`name`, `email`, `image`).
4.  Leave all checkboxes ticked (`Create migration`, `Create model`, etc.) to generate everything.
5.  Submit and copy the generated route into `app/Admin/routes.php`.

### Integrating an Existing Model (e.g., 'User')
1.  Navigate to **Helpers > Scaffolding**.
2.  Fill in the names for the existing `User` model.
3.  **Untick** `Create migration` and `Create model` since they already exist.
4.  Keep `Create controller` and `Create new menu` ticked.
5.  Submit and add the new route to `app/Admin/routes.php`.

## Essential Configurations

### File Uploads
To enable file uploads, you must configure a dedicated filesystem disk.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> In `config/filesystems.php`, add the following `admin` disk to the `disks` array. Without this, file uploads will fail.
> ```php
> 'admin' => [
>     'driver' => 'local',
>     'root' => public_path('uploads'),
>     'url' => env('APP_URL') . '/uploads',
>     'visibility' => 'public',
> ],
> ```

### Image Display
To ensure images are displayed correctly in both forms and lists:

1.  **Update `.env` file:** Set the `APP_URL` to your full local development URL and **remove any trailing slash**. For example: `APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

2.  **Modify Controller:** In the generated resource controller (e.g., `StudentController.php`), modify the `grid` definition in the `grid()` method to render the image field as an image:
    ```php
    // Before
    $grid->column('image', __('Image'));
    
    // After
    $grid->column('image', __('Image'))->image();
    ```

## Introduction & Project Setup

Hello everyone, this is Iamin and in this tutorial, I'm going to show you how you can install an admin panel in your Laravel project really easily. In order to install the admin panel, you just need to write three or four lines of command and your admin panel will be installed. And after that, you'll be able to easily display, edit, delete, or update any data in the admin panel. So I'll show you everything step-by-step from the very beginning. So this is the admin panel we'll create in this project. So we'll be able to do a lot of things in this admin panel. So I'll just create a fresh Laravel project right now. So let me just go to the file manager over here, and let's say I'll create our project over here. So let me just write over here CMD, we'll just open a command prompt, and let's just get our fresh Laravel project. We are going to say over here `laravel new`, let's say project name will be `Lara-admin-panel`. You can give it any name. So we'll just press enter, so it will start creating our Laravel project. So right now I'll just fast-forward the video.

So here you can see our project creation is complete. And here is the project folder over here. So let's just run the project. So let's just go to the project directory: `cd Lara-admin-panel`, press enter. So partly in the project directory. So let's run our project: `php artisan serve`.

So right now, we'll just see this over here. So this is our fresh Laravel project.

So right now, we are going to install a Laravel package for this project. But before that, we need to create our database and migrate our table, whatever table we have. So, right now, let's just go and open another command prompt in the project directory. So I'll just go inside the project over here. So right now, let's just write over here CMD. We'll just open a command prompt again over here and let's just write the command over here: `php artisan migrate`. So it will just migrate all the table we have.

## Automated Database Creation

And it will ask us, "Would you like to create a database?" We will just say over here yes, and it will automatically create a database for us. Press enter.

So here you can see it just created some tables, and the database name will be our project name, which is `Lara-admin-panel`. So let me just show you the example. But here, let's just go to the XAMPP dashboard over here, phpMyAdmin. So this is our phpMyAdmin. So right now, let's just find the `Lara-admin-panel`. So here you can see `Lara-admin-panel`, and some table is migrated over here. Okay. So our basic preparation is done.
